assets.title: Collect feedback where it happens
assets.content:
Subject: Collect feedback where it happens
Preview text: Start with one focused question, then place the form on the page where it matters.

Ask the question on the page

Hi there,

Ask one focused product question at the point where someone is using the feature it concerns. They can respond there, without being sent to a separate form page.

Tally is an online form builder that lets you create the form first, then render it inline on your website. To embed it, add Tally’s widget script and an iframe with `data-tally-src` to the page.

Start with one question on one relevant page. It is a practical way to see how Tally fits your product-feedback loop before deciding where else a form would be useful.

You can create unlimited forms and submissions free while your use stays within Tally’s fair usage guidelines.

Create a free form → https://tally.so/create

- Tally

asset_metadata.single_idea: Tally lets a product team put a feedback form directly on its own page and start collecting submissions with unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines.

selected_brief.selection_reason: Embedded feedback collection is relevant across the selected product-team audience without assuming a particular destination or installed stack, and the documented free offer gives a new buyer a concrete reason to act now.

value_case.reader_benefit: A product team can place a feedback form directly on a website or product page and collect submissions without paying per form or submission while its use remains within Tally's fair usage guidelines.
value_case.mechanism: Tally renders the form inline through its widget script and an iframe, while its free offer includes unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines.
decision_conditions: The unlimited free offer is subject to Tally's fair usage guidelines.
The documented embed is the standard website widget-and-iframe mechanism and requires adding the widget script and an iframe with data-tally-src.

claim_conditions: Keep 'unlimited' attached to the fair usage condition.
Describe only the documented website iframe/widget embed, not native mobile or SDK support.
Add the Tally widget script (https://tally.so/widgets/embed.js) and an iframe with data-tally-src to the host page (R12).
A free Google account is required for the Google Sheets integration (R3).
A webhook endpoint must return a 2XX status within 10 seconds or the documented retry sequence applies (R13).

The embed documentation covers the standard website iframe/widget mechanism only and does not state native in-app mobile SDK support, and the free unlimited-submission offer is bounded by the fair use guidelines whose example threshold is 50,000 submissions/month sustained for 3-4 months.

selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: trying another form builder may mean meeting a paywall before a product-feedback workflow is useful. After: Tally can be used to create and embed the form, with unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines.
must_not_say: Do not claim Tally is free without the fair usage condition.
Do not describe 50,000 monthly submissions as a hard cap.
Do not promise higher response rates, more revenue, faster research, or better feedback.
Do not claim native mobile SDK or in-app mobile support.
Do not imply that every recipient uses Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets, Make, Zapier, or webhooks.
Do not claim Tally eliminates complex field mapping or conditional branches.
Do not make competitor comparisons or exclusivity claims.
Do not add the API, AI, security, GDPR, pricing, language, file-upload, version-history, or full integration catalogue arguments.
Do not make blanket legal or regulatory assurances.
Do not claim Tally Pro costs €20 per month or Tally Business costs €65 per month.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Tally offers an online form builder I could use to place a focused feedback question directly inside a product page, letting me test an in-context feedback loop without sending users elsewhere.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly places me on a SaaS/startup product team building feedback loops, so asking for feedback where a feature is used is relevant. The reported Tally-to-database routing behavior is only inferred market context; this email does not assume that I personally use Tally, Airtable, Make, or a webhook. Whether inline feedback is a current priority and whether this embed would fit our product are unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I work on a SaaS/startup product team concerned with building feedback loops.
Email-only: I have a product page where one focused feedback question would be useful.
Email-only: adding Tally's widget script and an iframe is acceptable in our product.
Email-only: avoiding a separate form page would improve our feedback collection.
Not established as my experience: using Tally, Airtable, Make, or an existing Tally-to-database workflow.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Collecting contextual product feedback is relevant to my role, but the profile does not establish that I currently need a new embedded form or have a deadline. This feels like a plausible, inexpensive experiment rather than an urgent problem.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: My main reservation is product fit: the email tells me how the form is embedded but not whether it can visually fit our interface or what the embedded experience actually looks like. That uncertainty is small enough that I would still inspect the free option.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had shown one concrete example or screenshot of a one-question form embedded on a SaaS product page.
fixes: Rewrite "Ask one focused product question at the point where someone is using the feature it concerns." to include a concrete example, such as asking for feedback immediately beneath a newly used feature.

After "To embed it, add Tally’s widget script and an iframe with `data-tally-src` to the page.", add a screenshot or a factual sentence explaining what control, if any, I have over the embedded form’s appearance.

Trim "Start with one question on one relevant page. It is a practical way to see how Tally fits your product-feedback loop before deciding where else a form would be useful." to "Test one question on one product page before expanding it elsewhere."

brief.reader:
Selected audience: SaaS/startup product teams building feedback loops.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): Teams that embed Tally forms report wiring form submissions through either a native integration or a Make.com webhook workflow into Airtable, i.e. the audience is already attempting the Tally-to-database routing step described in the candidate's situation hypothesis.
brief.reader_segment: SaaS/startup product teams building feedback loops
brief.promise: Tally gives product teams a form they can place on a product page and use to collect feedback, with unlimited forms and submissions free within its fair usage guidelines.
brief.orientation: Tally is an online form builder whose forms can be embedded in a product page and whose submissions route into Notion, Airtable, Google Sheets or a webhook endpoint, with unlimited forms and submissions free within its fair use guidelines.
brief.arc: In this one-email arc, introduce the product through one immediately useful operation, make the free offer concrete, qualify it honestly, and invite the reader to create their first form.
brief.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email needs one broadly relevant reason to try Tally, not a catalogue of integrations. The embed mechanism makes the product tangible for a product team, while the free unlimited-forms-and-submissions offer lowers the barrier to taking the requested next step. The narrower Airtable proposition is retained as a complete alternative because it is especially relevant to the researched subsegment, but it should not become the primary premise for recipients whose stack is unknown. The single thing that would most change this campaign: can the source at https://tally.so/ be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: Embedded feedback collection is relevant across the selected product-team audience without assuming a particular destination or installed stack, and the documented free offer gives a new buyer a concrete reason to act now.

value_case.reader_benefit: A product team can place a feedback form directly on a website or product page and collect submissions without paying per form or submission while its use remains within Tally's fair usage guidelines.
value_case.mechanism: Tally renders the form inline through its widget script and an iframe, while its free offer includes unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines.
decision_conditions: The unlimited free offer is subject to Tally's fair usage guidelines.
The documented embed is the standard website widget-and-iframe mechanism and requires adding the widget script and an iframe with data-tally-src.

claim_conditions: Keep 'unlimited' attached to the fair usage condition.
Describe only the documented website iframe/widget embed, not native mobile or SDK support.
Add the Tally widget script (https://tally.so/widgets/embed.js) and an iframe with data-tally-src to the host page (R12).
A free Google account is required for the Google Sheets integration (R3).
A webhook endpoint must return a 2XX status within 10 seconds or the documented retry sequence applies (R13).

The embed documentation covers the standard website iframe/widget mechanism only and does not state native in-app mobile SDK support, and the free unlimited-submission offer is bounded by the fair use guidelines whose example threshold is 50,000 submissions/month sustained for 3-4 months.
emails.target_audience: SaaS/startup product teams building feedback loops
emails.job: Get a new buyer to create a free form for a product-feedback use case.
emails.single_idea: Tally lets a product team put a feedback form directly on its own page and start collecting submissions with unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines.
emails.mechanism: The team creates a Tally form, then the documented widget script and iframe render it inline on the team's page. Tally's free offer covers unlimited forms and submissions within its fair usage guidelines.
emails.belief_shift: Before: trying another form builder may mean meeting a paywall before a product-feedback workflow is useful. After: Tally can be used to create and embed the form, with unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines.
must_not_say: Do not claim Tally is free without the fair usage condition.
Do not describe 50,000 monthly submissions as a hard cap.
Do not promise higher response rates, more revenue, faster research, or better feedback.
Do not claim native mobile SDK or in-app mobile support.
Do not imply that every recipient uses Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets, Make, Zapier, or webhooks.
Do not claim Tally eliminates complex field mapping or conditional branches.
Do not make competitor comparisons or exclusivity claims.
Do not add the API, AI, security, GDPR, pricing, language, file-upload, version-history, or full integration catalogue arguments.
Do not make blanket legal or regulatory assurances.
Do not claim Tally Pro costs €20 per month or Tally Business costs €65 per month.
Tally's Pro plan costs €20 per month
Tally's Business plan costs €65 per month
emails.objection: The reader may assume a useful feedback programme will require a paid plan once it has more than a few forms or submissions.
emails.tone: Plainspoken, confident, warm, and concise; mildly anti-paywall without attacking competitors.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Tally is a practical starting point for the team's next product-feedback form.
emails.next_step_value: The destination lets the reader create a Tally form under the documented free offer.
emails.next_step_limit: Creating a form does not by itself validate the website embed in the reader's environment or any downstream integration.
emails.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete opportunity to put product feedback on the team's own page, while making the free entry point clear without turning the subject into a feature list.

brief.voice_notes: Use short declarative paragraphs and speak as 'we.' Keep the product visible early. Avoid generic superlatives and end with — Team Tally.
